items.followUp: Why do ionic compounds generally have high melting points?

rubric.why: Identifies the strong attraction between oppositely charged ions.
rubric.description: Strong electrostatic attraction holds the ions together.
rubric.how: Award for linking the attraction to oppositely charged ions.

rubric.why: Explains why high temperatures are needed to melt or boil the compound.
rubric.description: A large amount of energy is needed to overcome these forces.
rubric.how: Award for stating that substantial energy is needed to separate the ions.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds contain positively and negatively charged ions held together by strong electrostatic forces of attraction.
A large amount of energy is needed to overcome these forces, so ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points.

items.followUp: Define diffusion and give one example.

rubric.why: Defines effusion as gas molecules passing through a very small opening.
rubric.description: Effusion is the escape of gas molecules through a tiny opening.
rubric.how: Award for identifying gas escaping through a small hole.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example of effusion.
rubric.description: Example: gas escaping from a container through a tiny hole.
rubric.how: Award for an example that demonstrates gas escaping through a small opening.

modelAnswer: Effusion is the escape of gas molecules through a very small opening into a region of lower pressure.
Example: gas escaping from a container through a tiny hole.

items.followUp: Why is air considered a mixture?

rubric.why: Identifies that a solution consists of substances physically combined, not chemically bonded.
rubric.description: A solution is a physical combination of two or more substances.
rubric.how: Award for describing the components as physically combined or not chemically combined.

rubric.why: Gives a characteristic that explains why a solution is a mixture.
rubric.description: Its components can be present in variable proportions and retain their properties.
rubric.how: Award for any valid mixture characteristic, such as variable composition or components retaining their properties.

modelAnswer: A solution is a physical combination of two or more substances, not a chemical combination.
Its components can be present in variable proportions and retain their properties; therefore, a solution is a mixture.

items.followUp: Name four metals that are highly reactive.

rubric.why: Checks that four metals from the least reactive group are named.
rubric.description: Names four least reactive metals: copper, silver, gold and platinum.
rubric.how: Award 0.5 marks for each correct metal, up to 2 marks.

modelAnswer: The four least reactive metals are copper, silver, gold and platinum.

items.followUp: State five physical properties of non-metals.

rubric.why: Identifies the lustrous appearance of metals.
rubric.description: Metals are generally lustrous (shiny).
rubric.how: Award for stating that metals are lustrous or shiny.

rubric.why: Identifies a characteristic mechanical property of metals.
rubric.description: Metals can be hammered into thin sheets (malleable).
rubric.how: Award for stating that metals are malleable.

rubric.why: Identifies another characteristic mechanical property of metals.
rubric.description: Metals can be drawn into wires (ductile).
rubric.how: Award for stating that metals are ductile.

rubric.why: Identifies metals' electrical conductivity.
rubric.description: Metals are good conductors of electricity.
rubric.how: Award for stating that metals conduct electricity well.

rubric.why: Identifies metals' thermal conductivity.
rubric.description: Metals are good conductors of heat.
rubric.how: Award for stating that metals conduct heat well.

modelAnswer: Metals are generally lustrous, or shiny.
They are malleable and can be hammered into thin sheets.
They are ductile and can be drawn into wires.
They are good conductors of electricity.
They are good conductors of heat.

items.followUp: Define boiling point and explain how pressure and impurities affect it.

rubric.why: Gives the definition of boiling point.
rubric.description: Boiling point is the temperature at which a liquid's vapour pressure equals the atmospheric pressure.
rubric.how: Award for relating the liquid's vapour pressure to atmospheric pressure.

rubric.why: Explains the effect of external pressure on boiling point.
rubric.description: Increasing external pressure raises the boiling point; decreasing it lowers the boiling point.
rubric.how: Award for correctly stating the direction of the pressure effect.

rubric.why: Explains the effect of a non-volatile impurity.
rubric.description: A dissolved non-volatile impurity raises the boiling point.
rubric.how: Award for stating that adding a non-volatile impurity raises the boiling point.

rubric.why: Recognises the effect of the forces between liquid particles.
rubric.description: Liquids with stronger intermolecular forces have higher boiling points.
rubric.how: Award for relating stronger intermolecular attraction to a higher boiling point.

modelAnswer: The boiling point is the temperature at which the vapour pressure of a liquid becomes equal to the atmospheric pressure.
Increasing external pressure raises the boiling point, while decreasing pressure lowers it.
A dissolved non-volatile impurity raises the boiling point.
A liquid with stronger intermolecular forces generally has a higher boiling point.

items.followUp: Give four characteristics of colloidal solutions.

rubric.why: Identifies the heterogeneous nature of a suspension.
rubric.description: A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a suspension is heterogeneous.

rubric.why: Identifies that suspension particles can be seen.
rubric.description: Its particles are large enough to be seen with the naked eye.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the particles are visible or large.

rubric.why: Identifies the settling of suspended particles.
rubric.description: The particles settle on standing.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the particles settle when left undisturbed.

rubric.why: Identifies a method for separating suspension particles.
rubric.description: The particles can be separated by filtration.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a suspension can be separated by filtration.

modelAnswer: A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.
Its particles are large enough to be seen with the naked eye.
The particles settle when the suspension is left standing.
The particles can be separated from the mixture by filtration.

items.followUp: How many protons and neutrons are present in a sodium atom ²³₁₁Na?

rubric.why: Checks that the atomic number is identified as the number of protons.
rubric.description: The phosphorus atom has 15 protons.
rubric.how: Award for the correct number of protons.

rubric.why: Checks the neutron calculation from mass number minus atomic number.
rubric.description: Neutrons = 31 − 15 = 16.
rubric.how: Award for the correct number of neutrons.

modelAnswer: Given: mass number, A = 31; atomic number, Z = 15.
Number of protons = Z = 15.
Number of neutrons = A − Z = 31 − 15 = 16.
Answer: the phosphorus atom has 15 protons and 16 neutrons.
